channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar climbs ahead of NZ employment data
item.description: NZD/USD trades on the front foot near 0.5886 on Wednesday, advancing around 0.3% and building on the rebound that lifted the pair off the 0.5850 area.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Trendline break puts 50-day SMA in focus
item.description: The USD/CHF retraced on Tuesday, down 0.16%, as the US Dollar weakened amid improved risk appetite, driven by renewed hopes of a US-Israel peace deal to open the Strait of Hormuz. The pair trades below 0.8100.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Strengthening toward 6.7300 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang sees USD/CNH trading slightly higher within a developing range, with intraday levels expected between 6.7500 and 6.7620. On a 1–3 week horizon, the pair could continue to edge lower toward 6.7300 as long as 6.7640 holds as strong resistance.

item.title: Vietnam Dong: Stable despite widening trade deficit – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts note that Vietnam’s July inflation eased to 4.5% year-on-year, keeping the average near the 4.5% target, while the trade deficit widened to USD 3.6 billion on strong import growth driven by energy and capital goods.

item.title: Nothing Britain does moves the Pound against the Dollar
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) trades near 1.3450 against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, higher by 0.11% inside a session range of 36 pips, the second sub-40-pip day cable has produced inside a week.

item.title: Forex Today: Oil extends collapse on Hormuz reopening reports, Silver surges
item.description: Oil prices extended their slide on Tuesday after reports that an announcement on the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz could come within hours.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Gains risk watched below 1.2790 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes USD/SGD’s recent downside bias has faded after a dip to 1.2790 and recovery to 1.2827.

item.title: Mexican Peso rallies to six-week high on Hormuz deal speculation
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) surges to a six-week high on Tuesday as talks between the US and Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz, easing global inflationary pressures by freeing ship traffic. At the time of writing, the USD/MXN pair trades at 17.26, after reaching a high of 17.33.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: PMI weakness boosts easing expectations – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank economist Dr. Henry Hao highlights that China’s private manufacturing PMI fell to 50.9 in July, reinforcing signs of slowing factory momentum alongside the official NBS PMI at 49.2.

item.title: British Pound: Range trade with upside risk against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s Global FX Strategy team notes that Sterling remains modestly firmer, with GBP/USD continuing to pivot around long-term moving averages near 1.34.

item.title: Gold shines and rises on Iran’s deal hopes, lower US yields
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) advances some 0.75% on Tuesday as Oil prices fall, along with US Treasury yields. Also, an improvement in risk appetite propelled the yellow metal to a two-day peak of $4,106.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: 200-day SMA caps rebound after intervention-led selloff
item.description: USD/JPY trades modestly higher on Tuesday despite a softer US Dollar (USD), as the impact of recent intervention fades and the Japanese Yen (JPY) comes under pressure again.

item.title: Indonesia: Trade risks and structural support – UOB
item.description: UOB economists Enrico Tanuwidjaja and Vincentius Ming Shen assess Indonesia’s June 2026 trade data, highlighting that the trade deficit narrowed as stronger non-oil and gas exports partly offset rapid import growth.

item.title: Bulldozers built a third of the Dow Jones Industrial Average record
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average trades above 54,100 on Tuesday, more than 900 points higher and through the July peak just over 53,300 that had stood since the first week of last month. The run reaches a fourth consecutive session and close to 2,500 points, near 5%, since the 29 July decision.

item.title: WTI Oil drops sharply after Bessent signals an imminent Iran deal
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil is falling sharply on Tuesday, trading around $75.70 per barrel at the time of writing, down 3.91% on the day and at its lowest level in the last three weeks.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Bullish signals point to gains versus US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) has lagged other G10 currencies despite a softer US Dollar (USD) tone and improving Canadian data surprises versus the United States (US).

item.title: British Pound rebounds as soft JOLTS and Oil decline pressure USD
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) recovers some ground against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, up 0.14%, as US jobs data was softer than expected but confirmed the strength of the labor market, with layoffs being little changed. The GBP/USD pair trades at 1.3451 after rebounding from 1.3419.

item.title: Euro holds above 1.1500 on Hormuz reopening hopes and softer US jobs data
item.description: EUR/USD holds firm above 1.1500 on Tuesday as traders assess the latest developments surrounding US-Iran talks and the possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Silver advances amid Hormuz reopening hopes
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades with a mildly positive tone near $59.50 per troy ounce on Tuesday, up 2% for the day, but falling from recent highs and leaving the metal locked in a tight range.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Rally questioned as safe-haven role tested – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley notes the US Dollar (USD) has been the weakest G10 currency over the past week, with US Dollar Index (DXY) down about 2% from late July.

item.title: Asia FX: Yen-led winners and export backdrop – MUFG
item.description: Michael Wan at MUFG explains that South Korean Won (KRW), Thai Baht (THB), Singapore Dollar (SGD) and, to a smaller extent, Philippine Peso (PHP) are the main Asian FX beneficiaries if Japanese Yen strength persists, given their higher sensitivity to USD/JPY.

item.title: Euro: Consolidation below resistance against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s analysts observe that the Euro is consolidating around the 1.15 area against the Dollar, with limited Eurozone data to drive price action.

item.title: Japanese Yen stalls amid soft JOLTS data
item.description: USD/JPY trades on the back foot near the 157.40 area during Tuesday's American session as the Japanese Yen (JPY) builds on the gains secured over the past week.

item.title: Canada: Trade surplus hits four-year high – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada’s (NBC) Jocelyn Paquet reports Canada’s merchandise trade surplus in goods reached a four-year high of C$3.86 billion in June, beating expectations.

item.title: Gold recovers as Hormuz reopening hopes drag US Dollar, Oil prices lower
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) catches a fresh bid on Tuesday as traders react to encouraging headlines about the possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,087, recovering from an intraday low near $4,042.

item.title: Fed's Paulson: Underlying inflation is too high
item.description: Anna Paulson, President of the Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of Philadelphia, said in an interview with CNBC on Tuesday that underlying inflation remains too high and that monetary policy needs to stay mildly restrictive, adding that the current environment likely meets that description.

item.title: Australian Dollar climbs above 0.7000 as hopes of an Iran deal lift risk sentiment
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.7035 on Tuesday at the time of writing, up 0.50% on the day. The pair is supported by improving market sentiment after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that an agreement with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be reached as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday.

item.title: United States: Growth impulse questioned – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered analysts Dan Pan and Steve Englander discuss the Federal Reserve’s Financial Conditions Impulse on Growth (FCI-G) index, noting it was highly accommodative in May 2026 and still supportive after the July FOMC.

item.title: United States JOLTS Job Openings decline to 7.35 million in June
item.description: The number of job openings stood at 7.359 million in June, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Tuesday. This print followed the 7.537 million openings reported in May and came in slightly below the market expectation of 7.4 million.

item.title: US Dollar: Dip after FOMC but strength expected – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists discuss the US Dollar (USD) reaction to the July Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, where the Federal Reserve (Fed) kept rates at 3.50-3.75% despite some dissent for a hike.
